classification.difficultyReason: Convert sector angles to population proportions, take a complement within the older male subgroup, and combine older groups with the middle-age percentage to find the remaining population before rounding.

content.prompt: The pie chart shows how $21\,000\,000$ Australians are divided into various groups according to age and gender. The angles of the sectors for ‘Females aged 65 years and above’ and ‘Males aged 65 years and above’ are about $26^\circ$ and $21^\circ$, respectively. Give your answers to the nearest $10\,000$.

spec.description: Unequal sectors require ordinary TikZ rather than the equal-sector fraction-circle template. Pie on the left, six-category legend on the right and title above. Unlabelled sector boundaries reproduce approximate source proportions; no inferred angles are printed.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise categories are youngest males, youngest females, middle-age males, middle-age females, oldest males and oldest females. The last two sectors represent approximately 21 degrees and 26 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied data display; no answers or calculated populations.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If $\frac{2}{3}$ of the ‘Males aged 65 years and above’ are under 70, how many males are 70 years of age or older?

answer.worked:
The fraction aged 70 or older is $1-\frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$ of the males aged 65 or older.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Males aged 65 or older}&=\frac{21}{360}\times21\,000\,000\\\text{Males aged 65 or older}&=1\,225\,000\\\text{Males aged 70 or older}&=\frac{1}{3}\times1\,225\,000\\\text{Males aged 70 or older}&=\frac{1\,225\,000}{3}\\\text{Males aged 70 or older}&\approx410\,000\end{align*}$$

To the nearest $10\,000$, approximately $410\,000$ males are aged 70 or older.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $67\%$ of Australians are aged between 15 and 64 years, how many Australians are 14 years of age or younger?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Australians aged 65 or older}&=\frac{26+21}{360}\times21\,000\,000\\\text{Australians aged 65 or older}&=\frac{8\,225\,000}{3}\\\text{Australians aged 15 to 64}&=\frac{67}{100}\times21\,000\,000\\\text{Australians aged 15 to 64}&=14\,070\,000\\\text{Australians aged 14 or younger}&=21\,000\,000-14\,070\,000-\frac{8\,225\,000}{3}\\\text{Australians aged 14 or younger}&=\frac{12\,565\,000}{3}\\\text{Australians aged 14 or younger}&\approx4\,190\,000\end{align*}$$

Approximately $4\,190\,000$ Australians are aged 14 or younger, to the nearest $10\,000$.
